newsitem.title: USA: Texas wheat emergence stays ahead of average pace.
newsitem.headline: Texas wheat emergence stays ahead of average pace.

text.p: Emergence of winter wheat in Texas remained sharply ahead of average during the week ended Sunday, the weekly state crop report said.
Harvesting of corn was nearing completion in the Texas Plains, with above-average yields being reported. But wet weather last week in the Plains slowed some harvesting operations there.

Cotton harvest continued in full swing in North Texas and was nearing completion in south central Texas and the Upper Coast region. Some damage was reported to immature bolls as a result of a freeze in the Plains.
Wheat planted 95 percent vs 91 week ago, 79 year ago, 80 on a five-year average.
Wheat emerged 87 pct vs 78 w/a, 58 y/a, 62 avg.
Corn harvested 97 pct vs 94 w/a, 96 y/a, 98 avg.
Sorghum harvested 75 pct vs 71 w/a, 90 y/a, 87 avg.
Sorghum mature 99 pct vs 97 w/a, 99 y/a, 97 avg.
Sorghum rated 59 pct good/excellent vs 66 w/a.
Cotton bolls opening 91 pct vs 87 w/a, 83 y/a, 83 avg.
Cotton harvested 28 pct vs 24 w/a, 43 y/a, 41 avg.
Cotton rated 50 pct good/excellent vs 49 w/a.
Pasture and range condition was rated 31 pct good to excellent, versus 46 percent at that level last week.
